title: Precedence inversion in routing policy caused regional failover cascade
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-14 ~03:27 UTC we observed a cascade of cross-region failovers and repeated model-variant mismatches for hosted API traffic. A recent change to the routing policy evaluator introduced a precedence inversion between region affinity and variant compatibility checks. Combined with an off-by-one TTL regression in sticky-affinity caching, traffic oscillated between regions and hit incompatible model variants, causing elevated 5xx errors and 3–6x p95 latency for affected requests. Impact: ~12% of request volume for eu-west-1 routed customers experienced elevated latency and errors for ~45 minutes, several production customers reported degraded response quality or timeouts. This ticket tracks action items, investigation notes, and the fix rollout plan.
timeline: 2026-02-14 03:27 UTC - First spike observed: p95 latency for eu-west-1 increased from 190ms to 1.2s; error rate (5xx) rose from 0.2% to 4.1%.
2026-02-14 03:30 UTC - Automated policy fallback triggered due to regional capacity signal; routing engine started applying fallback chains.
2026-02-14 03:34 UTC - Engineering on-call triaged; noted repeated cross-region hops recorded in request trace headers (x-rw-route-hops).
2026-02-14 03:40 UTC - Containment: disabled new policy evaluator rollout (flagged) and forced explicit region pin for active customers to stop oscillation.
2026-02-14 03:58 UTC - Immediate reduction in hop count; error rate returned to baseline over next 10 minutes.
2026-02-14 04:10 UTC - Began rollback of sticky-affinity cache change to restore previous TTL semantics.
2026-02-14 05:05 UTC - Incident declared mitigated; paged owners for postmortem follow-up.
2026-02-15 10:00 UTC - Postmortem meeting: root cause assigned and action items prioritized.
root_cause: A regression in PR #8142 changed the evaluator ordering so that route->region->variant checks were evaluated in an inverted precedence under a specific codepath (when route had dynamic weight overrides). This resulted in the evaluator selecting a region-agnostic variant earlier than the compatible regional variant logic. Separately, a recent change to sticky-affinity caching (PR #8279) introduced an off-by-one TTL update when merging affinity entries, allowing affinity to expire earlier than intended and enabling frequent reroutes. Together they allowed cross-region reroute loops to form and exposed incompatible model variants to traffic.
contributing_factors: Lack of matrixed unit tests covering route/region/variant precedence with weight overrides
No e2e canary for policy-evaluator rollout; feature flag was enabled broadly before metrics validation
Telemetry did not include a specific 'precedence-mismatch' counter; detection relied on error spikes rather than policy signals
Affinity cache TTL regression was subtle and not captured by existing cache correctness tests
resolution_summary: Rolled back the policy evaluator change (flagged off) and reverted the sticky-affinity TTL change as immediate containment. Subsequent hotfix rebuilt the evaluator with corrected precedence logic and added defensive checks preventing selection of variant-incompatible routes. Hotfix deployed to hosted clusters 2026-02-15 02:12 UTC. Customer-facing incidents page updated; affected accounts contacted by Success. No Dedicated/Private customers were impacted.

notes: We must treat precedence logic as high-risk: small changes can cascade across routing and fallback layers. Immediate priorities are telemetry and test coverage to avoid silent regressions during future optimizations. The circuit-breaker design should be conservative to avoid disrupting valid cross-region failovers when capacity is legitimately unavailable.
